title: Philosophy / Principles

location.series: IBM Design Language / public web guidelines
location.extent: Complete webpage content-area capture; interactive elements retain their captured state

slide_intent: Turn an abstract ethos into questions that people can use when judging work, so craft and continuity remain deliberate decisions.
strategic_value: Four named principles can help distributed IBM teams assess whether an experience is useful, recognizable, carefully made and progressive.
demonstration: Four vertically stacked sections pair short principle names with explanations and practical review questions.
practical_value: Use the four question groups to review an execution’s purpose, relationship to the system, craft and contribution.

content_islands.name: Introduction
content_islands.spec: Place the Principles title above a short statement identifying designers and non-designers as the audience.

content_islands.name: Carefully Considered
content_islands.spec: Pair the first left-column principle with questions about utility, resources, gratuitous elements and respect for time.

content_islands.name: Uniquely Unified
content_islands.spec: Pair the next principle with questions about reusable solutions, recognition without the logo and relationships between experiences.

content_islands.name: Expertly Executed
content_islands.spec: Follow with craft questions about improvement, expertise, detail and the care visible in the experience.

content_islands.name: Positively Progressive
content_islands.spec: Close with questions about advancement, confidence, ingenuity and obstacles to understanding.

reference_purposes.Intent: The introduction says the principles establish criteria for conception, craftsmanship and creativity; each principle explains its underlying judgment.
reference_purposes.Application: Each section provides explicit questions to apply when reviewing design.
